newsitem.title: ITALY: Tempers fray after further delay on Italy's trains.
newsitem.headline: Tempers fray after further delay on Italy's trains.

text.p: Italy's government stood by its embattled transport minister on Tuesday but another incident on the country's archaic rail network caused a serious delay and provoked angry passengers to smash train windows.

Transport Minister Claudio Burlando emerged from a meeting with Prime Minister Romano Prodi and president of the state railway Giancarlo Cimoli and said he had appealed for more funds for the crisis-hit network.
"Cimoli and I asked, independendently from the budget, for a long term investment programme for the state railway," he told a news conference.
Burlando, who received Prodi's backing during the meeting, has been under pressure to resign following a series of rail accidents.
On Saturday a train jumped the tracks in Rome, injuring four passengers, and then a crane working to remove it collapsed on Sunday, blocking the lines which connect north and south Italy.
On Monday, an express train slammed into a car on a level crossing on the Rome-Naples line, killing three people, one of them a pregnant woman.
The official manning the crossing has been placed under investigation for manslaughter.
Rail traffic started to return to normal on Tuesday and engineers said they had reopened the lines through Rome which had been blocked by the crane.
But no sooner had Burlando told reporters he was working to improve Italy's creaking rail network, when another incident caused the temporary closure of the Rome-Naples line.
Engineers halted trains after a member of the public said he saw bits of a road bridge fall onto the track.
Trains were kept waiting for more than 1 1/2 hours while the lines were searched, prompting exasperated passengers in one train to smash the windows of their carriage.
It was unclear whether anything was found on the lines and by late evening the line had reopened.
The state railway promised earlier on Tuesday to compensate passengers for the weekend's havoc, offering a free ticket to anyone who could prove they travelled by train through Rome and Naples.
The far-right National Alliance has said it will call a vote of no-confidence in Burlando when parliament reopens in September.
"Prodi, Burlando and their party are directly responsible for these disasters. They have to own up to their political and personal responsibilities," Alliance official Maurizio Gasparri said.

Burlando said on Monday it would take five years for Italy's backward railways to reach the technological levels seen in other European countries, and that the government planned to invest some 42 trillion lire ($23 billion) in the network.
